what_was_done.result: Class B QA_ROUND_OUT_OF_ORDER predicate is the canonical guard. Refusals log + emit reconciler-action-refused event + return without calling addLabelsToEpic. Universal A.5 (BD_STATUS_DEFERRED / BD_STATUS_CLOSED) and Class-C (OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING / REVIEW_NEEDS_HUMAN) predicates also fire — load-bearing for the 372-bead mass-defer.

Selected because Class B qa-round-monotonic registers ONLY for ACTIONS_QA_ROUND_PROGRESSING ({send-for-qa, qa-fix-and-retest}). The rule itself does not dispatch this action — it consults the precondition library against the CONCEPTUAL action it is reacting to (the next QA round dispatch the system would otherwise perform). Mirrors the marker-driven-routing × dispatch-preconditions wiring shape established in beads_web-ehp.4.

deviations_from_ac: AC #3 (bead description: 'GIVEN route returns 412, WHEN act() receives it, THEN log + return without throwing') is structurally N/A for repeated-qa-round.ts. The rule's act() performs no HTTP fetch — its only side effect is addLabelsToEpic('review:needs-human'), which calls 'bd label add' directly via execFile (src/lib/pipeline-labels.ts:168-181), not via /api/fleet/action. The 412-handling AC was inherited from the marker-driven-routing pattern (beads_web-ehp.4) which DOES fetch /api/fleet/action; that pattern's HTTP defense-in-depth path does not apply here. Surfaced per the STOP-and-surface discipline (precedent: beads_web-1nm 2026-05-01); test file pins the documentation at the test boundary with a `test.skip` containing the rationale. Operator decision options: (a) accept-as-shipped (preferred — semantics correct, cross-rule pattern preserved); (b) extend the rule with a route fetch (changes behaviour — addLabelsToEpic becomes redundant or moves to a route action handler); (c) re-bead the AC text to remove the HTTP 412 clause for rules that don't fetch.
surprises_or_findings: (1) Architect prompt described 'snapshot re-read' before precondition; the rule's act() did not previously re-read (the snapshot used in match() was passed forward via match.context). The precondition gate's buildDispatchContext is ITSELF the snapshot read (calls readBeadStatus + readMarker + getEpicLabels) — no separate re-read needed. (2) Architect RISK FLAG noted potential marker filename ambiguity (QA marker shape '<epicId>-qa-round-<N>.json'). Verified empirically against src/lib/dispatch-preconditions.ts:822-838 — the v1 predicate inspects ctx.marker (per-bead '<epicId>.json' loaded by buildDispatchContext) and treats it as a QA-round marker if stage='qa' OR bead_id matches /-qa-round-\d+/. The predicate's v1 limitation is documented in the precondition library (predicate falls open when ctx.marker doesn't carry qa-round metadata; route.ts:1665+ remains load-bearing). The integration test exercises the per-bead-marker surface (which is the surface buildDispatchContext actually populates) — not a synthetic <epicId>-qa-round-<N>.json fixture. This means the test passes against the predicate-as-implemented; if Wave-3 ehp.13 later refines buildDispatchContext to read the QA-round-specific marker, the test fixture should be updated alongside. (3) Test interaction surprise during early test development: when run as a full suite, the first test failed because reconciler idempotency state may have leaked across tests; resolved by ensuring each test uses a fresh temp repo (via makeRepo()) and unique epicId. Once isolated, all 4 active tests + 1 skip pass deterministically.
recommendation_for_next: Reviewer: verify that (a) the action-argument 'qa-fix-and-retest' is the right concept-marker for THIS rule's intent (the rule flags review:needs-human when QA can't converge — the next mechanical dispatch WOULD be qa-fix-and-retest, so the precondition library is gating that conceptual dispatch via Class B); (b) the AC#3 HTTP 412 deviation is acceptable given the rule's no-fetch architecture (option a in deviations_from_ac); (c) the test file's mock pattern matches marker-driven-routing.precondition-integration.test.ts (it does — same jest.mock structure for bead-status-reader / marker-reader / pipeline-labels). If reviewer agrees, advance to QA. If reviewer wants the rule to also fetch /api/fleet/action (e.g., dispatching run-coherence-agent to subsume coherence-escalation work), surface as a separate bead — that's a behavioural change beyond the bead's stated SCOPE.
